Throughput / SLA asks (negotiation points):
- Magnolia target: sustained minimum 45k tokens/sec across dedicated pool during business hours (NA peak window).
- Concurrency cap: want soft cap at 3,000 concurrent chat streams; hard cap only after agreed throttling policy.
- Burst policy: allow bursts up to 80k tokens/sec for 10-15 minutes at a time, with automated throttling back to baseline. Bursts should not trigger charge spikes without prior notice.
- Token billing/overage: wants capped overage rate and a 30% buffer credit for first two quarters of POC.
Latency SLOs:
- Target p95 per-token generation latency < 120ms for avg seq=512 under sustained baseline; urgent for UI snappiness.
- End-to-end p95 for typical chat round (prompt + generation) < 800ms target; fallback models acceptable if quality within 10% degradation.
Reserved GPU planning:
- Magnolia prefers H100-80GB (NVIDIA H100) but open to A100-80GB for initial POC to speed timeline.
- Internal ask: initial reservation estimate = 8x H100-equivalent nodes for steady state; +2 hot nodes for burst/buffer. Expect to scale to 12 nodes in next 6-9 months with traffic growth.
- Planning constraint: colocated VPC in us-east that must pass network egress review; infra team will provide peering docs by 2026-03-10.
Routing & fallback preferences:
- Primary model: re-ranked llama-finetuned variant (higher quality), fallback to quantized 4-bit variant for bursts when latency tightens.
- Require automatic routing by policy (latency first in support chats; cost-first for non-real-time batch reranks).
Quality guardrails / evaluations:
- Magnolia will supply 1k QA prompts for regression checks. Wants Redwood Optimize to run model/quantization suggestions and report expected quality delta.
Commercial / legal considerations:
- SLA negotiation points: minimum tokens/sec guarantee, defined measurement windows (15m rolling), remedies (service credits) for missed SLOs rather than refunds.
- Data residency: US-only; Redwood private control plane option preferred. KMS integration required for customer-managed keys.
Open technical questions (for SE/Infra):
- How does Redwood measure aggregate tokens/sec across pooled GPUs? (per-shard aggregation vs per-node) — Magnolia wants deterministic measurement to avoid disputes.
- What is the enforced behavior when burst pool exhausted? Graceful queueing, prioritized throttling, or automatic fallback?
- Network egress baseline — expected throughput per H100 node under average load (SE to provide matrix).
